topics.lesson_subject: Multus CNI multi-network pod IP discovery in Kubernetes SDN connectors
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Kubernetes SDN connector parses network-status and network-extra-info pod annotations to discover primary and secondary Multus IPv4/IPv6 addresses and populate dynamic firewall address objects.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate API connector token -> Kubernetes API on configured server/port -> pod annotation read -> connector filter evaluation -> dynamic firewall address/address6 list refresh -> firewall policy object reference.
topics.failure_class: Incomplete dynamic address inventory when secondary attachment metadata, filter, address family, connector credentials, or API reachability is wrong.
topics.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdn status proves connector health; View Matched Addresses and show firewall address/address6 prove resolved IP members; neither alone proves the consuming policy matched a session.
topics.remediation_path: Validate Kubernetes API endpoint/token/certificate, both Multus annotations, pod-name filter, private/public collection scope, and configure IPv6 dynamic addresses in CLI.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate connector-up from complete secondary-network address discovery and identify why a Multus pod's second IPv6 address is absent.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate SDN connector to Kubernetes API, one pod with eth0 plus two Multus attachments, annotation plane feeding separate IPv4 and IPv6 dynamic address objects.

topics.lesson_subject: Global ADOM and policy-block distribution of IPv4/IPv6 local-in policies
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 allows local-in header/footer policies in Global Database ADOM and global/local policy blocks, then assigns the resulting policy package across multiple ADOMs.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Feature Visibility -> create IPv4/IPv6 local-in header/footer policy in Global Database ADOM -> append reusable policy block or global package -> assign to ADOMs -> install to managed FortiGates -> verify target local-in table.
topics.failure_class: Central policy absent or incorrectly ordered because feature visibility, policy-block append, global package assignment, ADOM scope, or install step is missing.
topics.evidence_pattern: Global flag and policy-block membership prove central object composition; install preview/read-back and target FortiGate local-in policy list prove delivery; a saved FortiManager object alone does not prove installation.
topics.remediation_path: Enable Local In Policies in Feature Visibility, confirm Global Database ADOM, append correct header/footer block, assign package to intended ADOMs, review install preview, and install.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish a global local-in policy object from a transit firewall policy and determine which packaging/assignment step makes it effective across ADOMs.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Global Database ADOM with reusable policy block feeding two global policy packages, assigned to separate local ADOMs and installed to FortiGate A/B.

topics.lesson_subject: SOC Automation Service content-pack entitlement, FDS delivery and object provenance
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Licensed Security Automation Service receives monthly RHSP/FortiGuard content packs containing premium reports, advanced correlation rules, alert handlers, SIEM parsers and connectors; eligible packs auto-apply from FDS.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: License validation and FortiCare entitlement -> FDS availability -> automatic pack application -> SOC Automation inventory -> object lookup by config type -> environment-specific connector configuration.
topics.failure_class: Expected pack or object missing because license, FDS reachability, FortiCare contract, minimum FortiAnalyzer version, or object-specific configuration is incomplete.
topics.evidence_pattern: License Information widget proves entitlement; SOC Automation table version/release/status proves pack inventory; Origin=FortiGuard proves provenance; none proves a connector is configured or parser is matching logs.
topics.remediation_path: Verify license and support entitlement, FDS connectivity, pack minimum version, SOC Automation inventory, then locate object in Reports/Alert Handlers/Log Parsers/Active Connectors and configure connector credentials.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify why a FortiGuard parser is visible in a content pack but external logs remain unparsed, and distinguish entitlement from connector activation.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGuard Distribution Server monthly content pack flows into licensed FortiAnalyzer; pack branches to global reports, alert handlers, parsers and connectors with provenance labels.

topics.lesson_subject: Active-active layer-3 routing within MCLAG using VRRP and BGP/OSPF
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: VRRP virtual IP/virtual MAC on both MCLAG peers combines with eBGP north/south and iBGP across the ICL so both peers hold routes and route ingress locally; FortiSwitchOS 8.0 adds IPv6 support.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure MCLAG/ICL trunks -> build north/south SVIs on both peers -> enable VRRP virtual MAC and peer-specific priorities -> eBGP to routers via VRRP VIP with multihop TTL 3 -> iBGP across ICL -> install routes on both peers.
topics.failure_class: ICL hairpinning, asymmetric route availability, VRRP virtual-MAC lookup failure, or no eBGP adjacency due to VIP/multihop/peer configuration mismatch.
topics.evidence_pattern: VRRP master/backup state, eBGP and iBGP neighbor state, route table on both peers, and traffic/ICL counters together prove active-active routing; one established neighbor does not prove both peers have forwarding state.
topics.remediation_path: Configure both MCLAG peers, enable vrrp-virtual-mac, use correct VRRP VIP and multihop TTL 3, establish iBGP across ICL, verify routes on both, and observe ICL transit.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why a VRRP backup can route locally without sending traffic over the ICL and identify the required virtual-MAC/iBGP dependency.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Northbound router and southbound router connected through Core1/Core2 MCLAG pair; peer ICL carries iBGP control routes while both cores perform local data-plane forwarding.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiAP isolated Configuration mode for initial deployment and recovery
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A 5-10 second reset-button press while booted enters temporary local configuration mode with serial-derived open SSID, NAT internet access, one Wi-Fi client, 1 dBm transmit power, no controller SSIDs, and 30-minute/reboot exit.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Booted AP -> timed reset-button gesture -> AP reboot into isolated config mode -> one client joins FAP-config-serial -> HTTPS GUI at 192.168.100.1 or CLI -> save -> reboot -> settings take effect.
topics.failure_class: AP unreachable for local setup because reset duration is wrong, AP is not booted, wrong SSID/client count, low transmit power, or configuration not committed/rebooted.
topics.evidence_pattern: FAP-config SSID and CONFIG MODE banner prove local mode; saved configuration and post-reboot behavior prove application; Wi-Fi association alone does not prove settings were committed.
topics.remediation_path: Use exact 5-10 second timing, connect one nearby client, access 192.168.100.1, save with OK or cfg -c, reboot, and avoid >10 seconds which factory-resets.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish reboot, configuration mode and factory reset by reset-button timing and predict why a second client cannot join.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: AP transitions from managed state into isolated temporary open NAT SSID, one local client configures it, then reboot returns AP to managed/controller discovery.

topics.lesson_subject: MultiKnownHostEntries for SSH polling through device VIP failover
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4.3+ per-device-model MultiKnownHostEntries allows multiple SSH host keys for the same modeled VIP and checks all matching known_hosts entries after VIP ownership changes.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Learn SSH keys from each possible VIP owner -> duplicate/associate each owner key to VIP -> verify multiple VIP entries in /bsc/.ssh/known_hosts -> enable MultiKnownHostEntries on modeled VIP -> subsequent SSH polls select matching key.
topics.failure_class: SSH CLI polling fails after VIP failover because the new active device presents a different host key than the single cached VIP key.
topics.evidence_pattern: Two known_hosts entries for the VIP prove candidate keys are installed; enabled attribute proves multi-entry lookup is enabled; successful CLI poll after failover proves correct key selection, not credential privilege.
topics.remediation_path: Preload key from every possible VIP owner, associate each to VIP, verify two or more distinct entries, enable the attribute for the device model, and retest failover.
topics.question_fingerprint: Diagnose a FortiNAC SSH poll failure that begins only after a VIP owner changes and choose a host-key trust fix rather than weakening SSH verification.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two controller devices with distinct SSH host keys share one VIP; FortiNAC device model points to VIP and known_hosts stores both key candidates.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F appliance 802.3ad LAG versus active/standby redundant interface groups
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 adds appliance LAG support; aggregate interface uses IEEE 802.3ad/802.1ax and LACP active/passive for multiple active links, while redundant interface groups use one link at a time.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select unused physical ports -> configure aggregate or redundant logical interface -> set LACP mode and member ports -> configure allowaccess/IP as needed -> match switch-side LACP trunk -> verify member negotiation and failover.
topics.failure_class: LAG remains down or degrades to a single member because member ports are in use, peer switch LACP is mismatched, or redundant mode is mistaken for bandwidth aggregation.
topics.evidence_pattern: Logical interface configuration proves intended membership; LACP actor/partner state and per-member counters prove negotiation and forwarding; one reachable IP does not prove all links are active.
topics.remediation_path: Remove ports from existing use, configure matching LACP active/passive settings on peer, verify member state, and use redundant mode only when one-active-link behavior is intended.
topics.question_fingerprint: Choose between aggregate and redundant interface types for a FortiNAC appliance requiring both increased bandwidth and link-level failover.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC appliance lag0 with port2/port3 active LACP members connected to a switch port-channel, contrasted with a separate one-active-link redundant group.

topics.lesson_subject: FIDO authentication requirements for IdP-initiated SAML portal logins
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0+ SAML IdP general settings can require FIDO for IdP-initiated login, choosing FIDO-only or password+FIDO and optionally allowing password+OTP only when all user FIDO keys are revoked.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User opens FAC IdP portal -> username-only page -> FIDO/password+FIDO validation -> authorized SP list filtered by SP group rules -> user selects SP -> FAC issues signed SAML assertion -> SP validates ACS response.
topics.failure_class: IdP portal login blocked or SP absent because no registered FIDO key, FIDO disabled/revoked, SP lacks IdP-initiated support, or user fails SP group authorization.
topics.evidence_pattern: FIDO authentication logs prove factor validation; SP portal visibility proves group-filter authorization; successful SAML ACS response proves assertion delivery, not downstream application authorization beyond SP.
topics.remediation_path: Register and enable FIDO keys, select correct FIDO mode/fallback, enable IdP-initiated assertion response on SP, verify group filters and signing certificate.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish FIDO factor failure from an SP hidden by group authorization and select the proper IdP-initiated SAML remediation.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser to FortiAuthenticator username-only portal and FIDO challenge, then filtered SP catalog, signed SAML assertion to SP ACS.

topics.lesson_subject: Terraform provider lifecycle for FortiPAM folders and secrets
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM Terraform provider manages folder and secret resources with CRUD/import using a REST API user token and typed secret-template fields.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create Standard API user -> generate one-time API token -> configure provider base_url/access_token/TLS verification -> terraform init -> plan -> apply folder/secret -> update/import/destroy with state tracking.
topics.failure_class: Provider authentication or resource drift because API user privilege/token is wrong, TLS validation disabled, template fields mismatch, or state/import exposes sensitive secret values.
topics.evidence_pattern: Terraform plan shows intended resource diff; apply output and FortiPAM object readback prove provisioning; state file contains plaintext imported secret fields and must be treated as sensitive.
topics.remediation_path: Use least-privilege API user, protect one-time token, enable TLS verification, pin provider version, review plan, encrypt/restrict state backend, and rotate exposed credentials.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify why a Terraform import is a secret-exposure event and distinguish provider resource CRUD from general FortiPAM session management.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Terraform configuration and protected state connect through REST API token to FortiPAM; folder and secret resources are created/updated/imported/destroyed.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM internal Case API for analyst lookup, case lifecycle and evidence attachment
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM 7.4+ public REST Case API exposes analyst lookup, create, update and attachment endpoints for native case-management objects, separate from external ITSM ticket synchronization.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Authenticate to Supervisor API -> GET analysts in organization/time scope -> POST case with summary/severity/assignee/incident IDs -> PUT updates and append notes/incidents -> POST attachment from IRI or /tmp path -> query case list/readback.
topics.failure_class: Case creation or evidence association fails due missing analyst, missing SP organization context, duplicate incident-to-case association, invalid attachment source, or mistaken expectation of external ticket sync.
topics.evidence_pattern: Create response caseId proves object creation; case list and incident association prove case linkage; attachment status proves upload; none proves external ITSM ticket was created.
topics.remediation_path: Define analysts, pass organization in SP mode, ensure incidents are not already attached elsewhere, use valid IRI or /tmp file path, and read back case and attachment.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate native FortiSIEM case creation from ticketing integration and diagnose a rejected incident association or attachment.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SOAR/SOC automation client calls analyst lookup, case create/update and attachment endpoints on Supervisor; case links incidents and stores evidence.

topics.lesson_subject: Mandatory change summaries for FortiSASE configuration audit logs
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: System Administration Require comments for configuration audit forces administrators to submit a change summary for configuration changes across objects, endpoint profiles and analytics/reporting.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable audit-comment requirement -> admin submits configuration change -> change-summary pane blocks commit until text is entered -> administrator event log records object/admin/description -> summary retained 30 days.
topics.failure_class: Change traceability gap because requirement disabled, operator omits summary, event-log indexing delay is mistaken for loss, or retention window expires.
topics.evidence_pattern: Administrator Events details show actor/object/summary; absence immediately after change may be indexing delay; audit summary does not prove approval or external change-ticket authorization.
topics.remediation_path: Enable Require comments, submit non-empty change summary, allow log propagation delay, review Administrator Events and export records within 30-day retention.
topics.question_fingerprint: Determine whether a missing administrator-event record means configuration failed, audit prompt disabled, or event indexing delay.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin submits config object change, mandatory summary gate precedes commit, then event pipeline records actor/object/summary into Administrator Events for 30-day review.

topics.lesson_subject: Application-signature learning and dynamic Lowest Cost SLA versus Best Quality steering
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Application Control/IPS recognizes application signatures and stores a destination IP/protocol/port 3-tuple in the application-control Internet Service ID list; subsequent sessions can match application-based SD-WAN rules using Lowest Cost SLA or Best Quality strategy.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Application Detection Based SD-WAN and policy Application Control -> first session inspected/classified -> 3-tuple cached -> SD-WAN app rule matches later sessions -> health-check metrics/cost/preference select member.
topics.failure_class: First session follows another rule or expected app rule misses because app not yet recognized, destination IP is not in cache, application control disabled, SLA fails, or member costs/preference misconfigured.
topics.evidence_pattern: application-control list proves recognized 3-tuple and cache freshness; health-check proves SLA measurements; service diagnostic proves selected members; none alone proves application signature for every destination IP.
topics.remediation_path: Enable feature visibility and Application Control, inspect app-control list, add relevant destinations/signatures, verify SLA participants/thresholds and member cost/preference, then retest subsequent sessions.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain first-session classification delay and choose Lowest Cost SLA versus Best Quality for business-critical versus noncritical applications.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client traffic enters FortiGate IPS/application classifier, application 3-tuple cache feeds SD-WAN service rule, SLA/cost ranking selects DIA1/DIA2/MPLS.
